answer: An agent marketplace selling ocean forecasts, juniper crop estimates, and jade appraisals requires each identity to lock a separate bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs. The protocol prevents one bond from backing multiple identities, so creating 1,000 eligible agents requires 1,000 bonds. Fake names remain cheap, but usable identities tie up capital: an attacker must fund the entire swarm and forgo other uses of that money until the lock expires.
